summary: A run.failed terminal whose error is missing/empty, over 4096 characters, or contains a run_/deleg_-like token raises in _consume_event instead of producing a FAILED terminal, so the genuine terminal is lost and the task session errors.
failure_scenario: Hermes reports status=failed (SSE run.failed and/or GET status) with error "", null, 5000 chars, or text such as 'failure at run_0123456789abcdef' -> _bounded_terminal_text raises RuntimeError; the stream handler's settlement re-polls and re-raises on the same payload -> BaseExceptionGroup is queued via _publish_failure -> next_update() raises, close() raises, and no work.completed(failed) is ever emitted although the run did terminate.
evidence: Ran an isolated aiohttp fake Hermes (scratchpad script reusing the test helpers _capabilities_response/_started_run_response/_dispatch_request) through the real HermesApiTaskSession start/dispatch/next_update. error='' , null, 'x'*5000, and a run_-id-bearing string each raised ExceptionGroup 'event stream failed with unresolved authority' from next_update and again from close(); control error='ok failure' yielded a FAILED terminal with reason 'ok failure'. The existing test only covers 'short' and 'over_controller_bound' (<=4096) error text. Frequency in production is not established; only reachable when Hermes emits such an error.

summary: render_presentation_response validates source_ids only for type, range and uniqueness, so a source in missing_source_ids (no passage supplied) can be rendered in the Sources footer as supporting the answer.
failure_scenario: Catalog has two URLs but only id 0 has a passage (missing_source_ids=[1]); the formatter returns source_ids [1] -> output ends 'Sources:\n<url 1>' and passes the terminal contract and the attestation, so the user sees a source that supplied no evidence for the answer.
evidence: Called render_presentation_response directly with a fake chat-completions response: ids [0] and [1] both render with the respective URL footer and no error. native_web_evidence.py:596-599 re-checks only that urls/passages did not change, not that selected ids carry passages. The prompt (evidence_presentation.py:72) tells the model missing ids have no passage but nothing enforces it. Needs a model to select the id, so reachability is model-dependent; the missing set is deterministic and already computed in presentation_input, so the check is not an English intent parser.

summary: _RUN_ID_DISCLOSURE matches any run_ + 16+ identifier characters with no word boundary (and any 'deleg_' substring), so ordinary operational identifiers make a valid completed result unusable.
failure_scenario: A completed task result mentioning scripts/run_release_gate_checks.py, prerun_configuration_snapshot, or a deleg_timeout option -> _completed_result_text returns the fixed 'could not be used' notice instead of the result. (Fail-closed; the matching private-id format is the narrower _RUN_ID_EXACT run_[hex]{16,64}.)
evidence: Executed HermesApiTaskSession._completed_result_text on a well-formed envelope: control accepted; each of the three strings returned the unusable notice. Leading/trailing whitespace around the envelope is also refused, which is the accepted exact-envelope limit, not a defect.

summary: Prior claim api.py:1750 (stripped length vs unstripped envelope): accepted tradeoff - exact envelopes intentionally reject surrounding whitespace; reproduced that a trailing newline yields the unusable notice, which is the documented fail-closed behavior.
Prior claim api.py:1266 (run.failed raises): reproduced; recorded as the first finding. Scope limit kept: no production frequency claimed.
Prior claim evidence_presentation.py:462 (unsupported source ids): reproduced at function level; recorded as the second finding, model-dependent reachability.

Prior claims on plugin.py, bridge.py, client/projection.py, service.py/test_hermes_service.py, preview_cutover.py and other files outside the assigned list were not examined for findings; plugin.py:150 and bridge.py:1022 are the same terminal-loss family as the first finding but their code was not reviewed here (unresolved: missing witness is a run of those modules).

web_evidence_contract.attestation_valid: checked exact field set, run/generation/output-hash equality, count bounds and per-disposition invariants; a 'refused' disposition report is rejected and converted to a failed terminal, fail-closed and consistent with api._web_completion. No defect found.

api._commit_terminal / _consume_event ordering: terminal commit is under the state lock with a capacity check before authority.terminal is set, so replayed or full-queue terminals do not mark the run terminal first. No defect found in the assigned paths.

presentation_transport and native_web_evidence: read the owner/cancel/deadline handling and the source-change recheck before publish; no substantiated defect found. Not exercised with real openai/httpx or native Hermes (static review only).

result_projection.py: _browser_safe_task_result / reference scrubbing read; no defect verified. Its run_ handle regex is wider (8+ chars) than api's (16+) and rewrites such tokens to 'private reference' without raising; treated as display-only.
